Forms · Kit part@kitora/pickers/ui

DatePicker

One date picker for every mode: a day, several days, a range, or one or a range of weeks, months, quarters or years, as ISO strings; with a time granularity a date-time or a date-time range (floating, a UTC instant or RFC 9557 zoned, in a display zone with a zone switch, a second-zone hint and fixed offsets), and time and time-range modes. Presets in every mode (rolling presets that stay relative to today), compare periods (previous period or year), nights or days, open-ended ranges, one field or two, ranges across disabled days, and range ends dragged by pointer or moved with Shift+arrows. Rules as data with reasons (weekdays, holidays, ranges, past or future only) shown on the day and announced, and async day data such as prices under the days. Typed segments or free text with natural language, calendar popover with a time list or columns, min / max bounds, clear, Apply / Cancel in every mode. Beside it the SlotPicker: free time slots from an availability adapter on the same calendar and zone parts, in a month or week layout. The pickers kit's DatePicker.

Source: @kitora/pickers (the single implementation; no other package ships one)

Anatomy

Which part renders inside which in the examples below, from @kitora/pickers/ui: each part's data-slot, the @kitora/primitives part it renders, its role, the state attributes it writes and the CSS variables it sets (style them with data-open:, data-checked: and the rest). Build your own builds the same thing from the parts alone.

Props

DatePicker

One date picker for every mode, plus its parts for composing your own (see file header).

  • valueDatePickerValue<M, G>

    Controlled value; null (or an empty range or list) is "nothing picked". Leave undefined for an uncontrolled picker.

  • defaultValueDatePickerValue<M, G>

    The value at first when uncontrolled.

  • openboolean

    Controlled open state; leave undefined to let the picker open and close itself.

  • defaultOpenboolean

    Default false

    Whether the picker starts open when uncontrolled.

  • onOpenChange(open: boolean) => void

    Called when the picker opens or closes, with the new open state.

  • onChange(value: DatePickerValue<M, G>, details: DatePickerChangeDetails) => void

    Called on every committed change, with the new value and where it came from.

  • inputDatePickerInput

    The field: segments (default) or text (formats plus natural language, previewed before Enter or blur commits). text works for a single date-time too ("15 dec 3:30 pm", "tomorrow at 9", the locale's own 12- or 24-hour time); a range or the time modes with a time keep the segments.

  • disabledboolean

    Default false

    Whether the picker is disabled.

  • maxIsoDate

    Latest selectable day, inclusive.

  • maxLengthnumber

    Range mode: the longest allowed range, in lengthUnit; time-range: minutes.

  • minIsoDate

    Earliest selectable day, inclusive.

  • minLengthnumber

    Range mode: the shortest allowed range, in lengthUnit (days count both ends); time-range: minutes.

  • readOnlyboolean

    Default false

    Whether the value is shown but cannot be changed.

  • nowIsoTime

    The current wall time for "Now"; default the host clock.

  • rulesreadonly DateRule[]

    Blocked days as data with reasons ({ weekdays: [0, 6], reason: "Closed on weekends" }, { dates }, { ranges }, { before }, { after }).

  • timeZonestring

    The display zone (IANA id or fixed offset like UTC+05:30), controlled; see the file header. Setting any zone option makes valueKind default to instant.

  • calendarCalendarId

    The calendar the day and week modes are drawn in: persian, islamic-umalqura, buddhist, japanese, hebrew or gregory; default the locale's -u-ca- extension, else Gregorian. The value stays an ISO Gregorian date; the grid, its labels and the displayed value are in the calendar, and the typed field keeps Gregorian numbers.

  • hourCycleHourCycle

    Force a 12- or 24-hour clock; default the locale's.

  • wordsParseWords

    The grammar's words; the styled picker passes the pickers catalog's (English PARSE_WORDS otherwise).

  • confirmboolean

    Default false

    Edit a draft and commit it with Apply (Cancel drops it); when false a pick commits.

  • localestring

    BCP 47 tag; default the browser's. Drives labels, the field order and the week start.

  • granularityG

    day (default) or a time precision: single and range then pick a date-time; the time modes default to minute.

  • closeOnSelectboolean

    Close when a pick completes the value; default true (multiple mode never closes on its own).

  • isDateDisabledDateDisabledFn

    Extra blocked days: true blocks, { reason } blocks and says why (shown on the day, spoken, and in the field's error).

  • disablePastboolean

    Block every day before today (the display zone's today).

  • disableFutureboolean

    Block every day after today.

  • dayDataDayDataLoader

    Async day data per visible month: labels under the days (prices), tones, blocked days with reasons.

  • dayDataKeystring

    Changing it drops the day data cache and ignores responses still in flight.

  • weekStartsOnWeekday

    Override the locale's first day of the week.

  • weekNumbersboolean | WeekNumbering

    A week-number column in the day calendar: true / "iso" (ISO 8601 weeks) or "locale" (the locale's week-of-year).

  • trimMonthsToMaxboolean

    Show no month wholly past max (the sheet's month scroller sets it, so it never runs past the last allowed month).

  • todayIsoDate

    "Today" for highlighting, presets and the default month; default the host clock.

  • numberOfMonthsnumber

    Default 1

    Months shown side by side in the day calendar.

  • anchorMonthAnchorMonth

    With several months, which one opens on today (or on a preset that fits one month) when nothing is picked: last (default) puts the past before it, as an analytics range wants; first puts the future after it, as the bottom sheet's vertical month scroller does.

  • pageBehaviorPageBehavior

    Page the day calendar by one month (single) or by every visible month (page).

  • outsideDaysOutsideDays

    The neighbouring months' days in the day calendar: selectable, visible (drawn, not pickable) or hidden.

  • fixedWeeksboolean

    Always draw six week rows so the surface never changes height; false drops rows outside the month.

  • lengthUnitLengthUnit

    Default "days"

    Range mode: count the range in days or nights (a 3-night stay spans 4 days; at least one night).

  • openEndedboolean

    Range modes: a value may keep one end ({ start, end: null }, "from 1 Jan"); default false.

  • allowsNonContiguousRangesboolean

    Range mode: a range may run across disabled days (both ends must be open); default false.

  • fieldsDatePickerFields

    Range modes: split (two fields, default for segments) or one (one field, default for input="text").

  • maxSelectednumber

    Multiple mode: the most days that may be picked.

  • presetsreadonly RangePreset[]

    Named ranges offered beside the calendar, in every date mode (presetsForMode(mode) gives the defaults); see the file header.

  • presetBehaviorPresetBehavior

    What a preset pick does; default accept (pick and close), stay with confirm.

  • rollingPresetsboolean

    Default false

    { start, end } modes: report a preset pick as { preset, start, end } and re-resolve such a value against today.

  • compareCompareKind

    Offer a compare period of this kind (DatePicker.Compare); the user can switch it off or to the other kind.

  • compareEnabledboolean

    Whether the compare period is on (controlled).

  • defaultCompareEnabledboolean

    Whether the compare period starts on; default false.

  • onCompareChange(enabled: boolean, kind: CompareKind) => void

    Called when the compare period is switched on or off or to the other kind, with whether it is on and its kind.

  • formatterCalendarFormatter

    Every calendar label and announcement; default the Intl formatter.

  • naturalLanguageboolean

    Default true

    With input="text", read natural language ("next fri", "last 30 days") as well as formats. The segment field's paste never does.

  • quarterLabelstring

    The quarter template for the text field (Q{quarter} {year}); the styled picker passes the catalog's.

  • minuteStepnumber

    Minutes between times: the list's interval (default 30) and the minute column's step (default 1).

  • secondStepnumber

    Seconds between second-column values at second granularity; default 1.

  • timePanelTimePanelView

    How the surface offers times: a list (default) or columns (default at second granularity).

  • minTimeTimeBound

    The earliest time that may be picked: one time for every date, or per date (null while no date is picked).

  • maxTimeTimeBound

    The latest time that may be picked (see minTime).

  • isTimeDisabled(time: IsoTime, date: IsoDate | null) => boolean

    Times that are taken or closed on a date (null in the time modes or before a date is picked).

  • timePresetsreadonly TimePreset[]

    Named times in the panel (DEFAULT_TIME_PRESETS: Now, Noon, End of day).

  • overnightboolean

    Default false

    time-range mode: an end before the start runs past midnight (a 22:00–06:00 shift); when false the end may not come first.

  • defaultTimeZonestring

    The display zone when uncontrolled; default the host's zone (when another zone option asks for one).

  • onTimeZoneChange(zone: string) => void

    Called when the display zone is switched, with the new zone.

  • zonePickerZonePickerMode

    A zone switch in the surface (DatePicker.ZoneSelect): true to switch, "locked" to show the zone fixed; default false.

  • valueKindDatePickerValueKind

    What a date-time value is: floating, instant (default with a zone) or zoned (RFC 9557).

  • disambiguationDisambiguation

    How a wall time a DST change skips or repeats becomes an instant (Temporal's; default compatible). reject commits the typed time with details.error and a null value.

  • secondaryTimeZonestring

    A second zone to show the picked time in ("9:00 AM New York = 7:30 PM Kolkata").

  • zoneDisplayZoneDisplay

    How the field shows the zone beside a date-time or time: short (default), offset or none.

  • timeZonesreadonly string[]

    The zones the zone switch offers (IANA ids or fixed offsets); default every zone the engine knows.

  • aria-labelstring

    The control's name; the range fields are "<label> start" / "<label> end".

  • aria-describedbystring

    Id of the element that describes the field (a hint or an error).

  • idstring

    Id for the field, so a <label for> can point at it.

  • namestring

    Posts the value with a surrounding <form>: the ISO string, a list joined by commas, or a range as start/end.

  • startNamestring

    Range modes: post the start and the end as two fields instead.

  • endNamestring

    Range modes: the form name the end posts under (with startName).

  • requiredboolean

    A surrounding <form> refuses to submit until the value is whole (a range: both ends, unless openEnded); focus moves to the field.

  • formstring

    The form the hidden inputs post into (a picker outside the <form> element).

  • invalidboolean

    Force the invalid look.

  • placeholderstring

    Shown in the read-only field and the button trigger while empty; default the catalog's "Pick a …".

  • sidePopoverSide

    Where the surface opens; default bottom, start.

  • alignPopoverAlign

    How the surface lines up with the trigger along side; default start.

  • surfaceDatePickerSurfaceOption

    The surface the panel opens on; default auto (see the file header).

  • sheetMonthsnumber

    Months the sheet's vertical scroller shows first and adds each time it is scrolled to its end (day and week modes); default {@link SHEET_MONTHS}.

  • modeM

    Default single.

  • childrenReactNode

    The parts (DatePicker.Field, DatePicker.Surface…) that read the picker state.

  • clearableboolean

    Show a clear (×) button when there is a value; default true.

  • footer(pick: (value: DatePickerValue<M, G>) => void) => ReactNode

    Extra content under the calendar (shortcuts like "Today"). Receives a function that sets the value and closes.

  • calendarClassNamesCalendarClassNames

    Per-part classes for the calendar in the surface.

  • classNamestring

    Extra classes for the field (the inline panel when surface is inline).

DateInput

A typed-segment date input: locale order, ↑/↓ to step, digits to type. No popover.

  • valueIsoDate | null

    Controlled day (null = empty); leave undefined for an uncontrolled field.

  • defaultValueIsoDate | null

    Default null

    Initial day when uncontrolled (null = empty).

  • onChange(value: IsoDate | null) => void

    Called when the day changes, with it (null when the field is cleared).

  • minIsoDate

    Earliest valid day; an earlier value turns the field invalid.

  • maxIsoDate

    Latest valid day; a later value turns the field invalid.

  • isDateDisabled(iso: IsoDate) => boolean

    Returns true for a blocked day; the field turns invalid on one.

  • localestring

    BCP 47 locale for the segment order and names; default the host's.

  • disabledboolean

    Whether the field is disabled.

  • readOnlyboolean

    Whether the field shows its value but cannot be edited.

  • invalidboolean

    Force the invalid look (the field also turns invalid on its own when the value breaks min/max/disabled).

  • aria-labelstring

    Accessible name for the field; default "Date".

  • aria-describedbystring

    Id of the element that describes the field (a hint or an error).

  • idstring

    Id for the field, so a <label for> can point at it.

  • namestring

    Posts the ISO value with a surrounding <form>.

  • classNamestring

    Extra classes for the field.

  • todayIsoDate

    "Today" for the T key and for + / − on an empty field; default the host clock.

  • onPasteText(text: string) => boolean

    Handles pasted text; return true when it did (default: one date in any accepted format).

  • endReactNode

    Trailing controls inside the field, after the segments (a clear or calendar button).

TodayButton

A ready-made footer button for DatePicker: jumps to today.

  • pickrequired(value: IsoDate) => void

    The pick function DatePicker's footer receives; called with today's date.

  • labelstring

    The button's text; default the catalog's "Today".

  • todayIsoDate

    Default today in the time zone in effect

    The day it picks, from the host clock (a HydrationDefaultsProvider's until hydration) unless given.

Hooks and functions

  • DATE_PICKER_SURFACES

    Where the picker's panel opens: auto picks sheet or popover by the viewport and the pointer.

  • dateOutOfBounds(value: IsoDate | null, min?: IsoDate, max?: IsoDate, isDateDisabled?: (iso: IsoDate) => boolean) => boolean

    True when value breaks the bounds or lands on a blocked day.

  • fieldErrorMessage(code: DateFieldError, picker: Pick<DatePickerState, "mode" | "isRange" | "unit"> & Partial<Pick<DatePickerState, "timeErrorOnly" | "timeZone">>, msg: PickersMessages, block?: DateBlock | null) => string

    The catalog's message for a field error; wrong-kind names what this picker takes.

  • formatPickerValue(picker: FormatPicker, value: DatePickerState["value"], msg: Pick<PickersMessages, "quarterLong"> & Partial<Pick<PickersMessages, "openFrom" | "openUntil">>, time?: TimeSelection) => string

    A value for display: a date, a list, a range, or a week, month, quarter or year (and their ranges); with time (a date-time or time picker's time half) the times too ("Nov 11, 2026, 2:30 PM", "9:00 AM – 5:00 PM").

  • presetLabel(preset: RangePreset, msg: PickersMessages) => string

    A preset's label: the catalog's text for a built-in preset that kept its English label, else the host's own label.

  • PRESET_LAYOUTS

    How the presets are laid out: a column beside the calendar, or a row of chips that scrolls sideways (the sheet's).

  • SHEET_MAX_MONTHS

    The most months the scroller grows to (it keeps the page light; the arrow keys still page past it).

  • SHEET_MONTHS

    Months the sheet's vertical scroller shows first, and adds each time it is scrolled to its end: half a year per thumb flick.

  • useDatePickerContext() => DatePickerContextValue

    The nearest DatePicker.Root's state; throws outside one so a misplaced part fails loudly.

01Default

Typeable field plus a calendar popover with a Today button.

mm/dd/yyyy
value: null

02Every mode

One DatePicker, eleven modes: single, multiple, range, and one or a range of weeks, months, quarters or years. The value is an ISO string (or a { start, end } range of them) and onChange(value, details) says where it came from.

yyyy-Www
onChange: none yet

03Weeks, months and quarters

mode="week" picks the locale's whole week as a day range (Sunday first in en-US, Monday in de-DE) with the ISO 8601 week id in details.isoWeek; mode="quarter" opens on four quarters (2026-Q4) and quarter-range spans years with the arrows or PageUp / PageDown; mode="month-range" with confirm previews the band on two clicks in either order and commits { start: "2026-01", end: "2026-03" } on Apply.

04Week numbers

weekNumbers adds a column of ISO 8601 week numbers ("locale" numbers by the locale's rule: in the US week 1 holds 1 January). The first day of the week and the tinted weekend columns come from Intl.Locale week info (Friday and Saturday in ar-SA), with a fallback for engines without it.

05Presets in every mode

presets work in every date mode; presetsForMode(mode) gives the default list (labels from the pickers catalog). A preset resolves to a day range and fits the mode: a day takes its start, a month the month around it, a range of quarters the whole quarters. presetBehavior="accept" picks and closes, "stay" picks and stays open; confirm adds Apply / Cancel in any mode.

06Analytics with compare

rollingPresets: a preset pick is stored as { preset, start, end } and re-resolved against today, so a saved "last 30 days" stays the last 30 days (this value was stored on 12 Nov). compare="previous-period" adds DatePicker.Compare: a switch, previous period or previous year, the compare range under the days and in details.compare.

lengthUnit="nights": a 3-night stay spans 4 days, the footer counts nights and minLength / maxLength (2 to 14) are nights. Sold-out nights cannot be inside a stay. Drag either end of the stay, or focus an end and press Shift+arrows to move it; the popover stays open.

10Date and time

granularity="minute" adds hour and minute segments and a time list beside the calendar; the value is a floating ISO date-time (2026-11-11T14:30). minTime / maxTime take a function of the day (opening hours), timePresets adds Now, Noon and End of day, and mode="range" with a granularity picks two date-times.

11Seconds

granularity="second" opens TimeColumns: hours, minutes, seconds, and AM/PM on a 12-hour clock. secondStep and minuteStep set the steps, hourCycle forces 12 or 24 hours; ↑/↓ and typeahead in a column, ← / → between columns.

14Meeting across zones

timeZone sets the display zone and makes the value a UTC instant (valueKind="instant"); zonePicker puts the TimeZonePicker in the surface (DatePicker.ZoneSelect), and switching it keeps the instant while the wall time shown changes. secondaryTimeZone adds "9:00 AM New York = 7:30 PM Kolkata", the field shows the zone (EST, or the offset with zoneDisplay="offset"), and on a DST day the list holds the zone's real times. The second picker shows the same instant on a fixed offset (UTC+05:30) and stores RFC 9557 (valueKind="zoned"); offset strings like 2026-07-01T09:30:00-04:00 are read too.

16DST days

A floating time has every wall time on every day. With timeZone and date, TimeList lists the times the zone really has: New York's spring day has 23 hours (no 02:xx), its fall day 25 (01:00–01:59 twice, EDT then EST, each reported with its instant). TimeColumns on the same day disables the gap's hour.

17Free text

input="text" reads the locale's formats: en-US 11/15/2026, en-GB 15/11/2026, de-DE 15.11.2026, plus month names and ISO. A pasted date or range works in either field kind, and while the text is unedited + and − step a day.

value: {}

18Typing a date and time

input="text" with a time granularity reads a date and a time together: 15 dec 3:30 pm, tomorrow at 9, 2026-11-15 15:30, and the locale's own clock, 12 or 24 hours, its AM/PM words before or after the time (오후 3:30 in ko-KR) and its separator (15.30 in fi-FI). The field shows the value the same way and reads it back; a time typed finer than the granularity is cut to it, and a date alone keeps the time the value has (or asks for one).

value: {"en-US":"2026-11-15T15:30"}

19Natural language

A grammar of our own, words in the i18n catalog: today, next fri, in 2 weeks, 15 dec 3pm, last 30 days, this month, q3. The line under the field shows the reading first; Enter or blur commits it with details.source: "parsed".

20Errors

Typed error codes with catalog messages: invalid and incomplete and wrong-kind keep the value; out-of-range and disabled commit and come back as details.error. Segments report the same codes; T, + and − work in both.

mm/dd/yyyy
last details.error: none

21Holidays with reasons

rules as plain data with reasons: { weekdays: [0, 6], reason }, { dates: [{ date, reason }] }, { ranges }, { before } / { after }, plus disablePast / disableFuture; isDateDisabled may return { reason }. A blocked day shows its reason under the grid and as a tooltip when hovered or focused, a screen reader reads it as the day's description, and a refused pick is announced. Months that are wholly blocked are disabled in the month grid. The form kit's dateRules validator checks the same data on the server.

22Price calendar

dayData: an async loader called once per visible month, here a fake fare service with a 700 ms delay. Labels (fares) sit under the day numbers, coloured by tone; sold-out days come back disabled with a reason. While a month loads its grid is aria-busy and the labels pulse; months are cached, a late answer for another month or an old dayDataKey (switch the currency) is dropped, and a failed load offers Retry.

23Popover or sheet

surface="auto" (the default) opens a popover from md up with a mouse, and the overlay kit's bottom sheet below md or on a touch screen: the one rule the form kit's fields use (useFieldOverlaySurface). On a touch screen the field turns read-only, so a tap opens the sheet instead of the on-screen keyboard, and every target is 44 px. The server always renders the popover variant.

24Bottom sheet

surface="sheet" at any width: the months stack in a vertical scroller that opens on today (or the value) and adds sheetMonths more as it reaches its end; the arrow keys run from one month into the next. Presets are a row of chips, and Apply / Cancel sit pinned under the scroller (confirm is on by default in the sheet). Tap the first night, the last, then Apply.

26Calendar systems

calendar="persian", "islamic-umalqura", "hebrew", "japanese" or "buddhist" (or a locale's -u-ca- extension) draws the grid in that calendar from the engine's Intl, no tables: its months (a Hebrew leap year has 13, Adar I and Adar II), its day numbers, a caption like Aban 1405 or Reiwa 8, paging and the month and year drill views. The value stays an ISO Gregorian date, so switching the calendar keeps it. Without calendar, fa-IR draws Gregorian months and names them as such.

fa-IR with the Persian calendar and ar-SA with Umm al-Qura inside dir="rtl": the chevrons point the reading way, ← moves to the next day, the range band and presets mirror, and the bottom sheet, the time columns and the week-number column follow the direction.

28Slot picker

SlotPicker puts free times on the same calendar and zone parts: an availability adapter ({ load(range) } answering the host's weekly hours in their zone, busy blocks and bookings), durations, rules (buffer, notice, horizon, max per day), the invitee's zone, Next available. Days with times are marked; a day without says so. The value is { start, end } UTC instants. More on /kits/pickers/scheduling: the week layout, seats left, a locked zone and the 12 / 24 h toggle.

29Design language

The theme kit's calendar slot draws every picker part: the cell size, corners, the selected fill and its shape (circle, square, rounded), how today is marked (ring, dot, bold, accent), the range band (band, pill, none), the weekday case, the caption row and the time row height. LanguageScope puts one picker in another language beside the page's own; its popover follows the scope. The field, popover, sheet and buttons read the input, popover, drawer and button slots.
